subject: Model catalog shortlist, context depth, and traffic multipliers — onboarding handoff
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finops.io>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: jason.reed@finops.io
Date: 2026-09-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow on context + volume (FinOps onboarding)

Vivek / Monica — thanks for the call today. Attaching the sample prompts and a small snapshot of Q3 traffic (high level) so you can size things. Two clarifications from product: 

- Typical user flow: user enters a billing query -> model does 1 pass of classification + 1 pass of long-form extraction when flag is set. Average raw prompt size ~ 320 tokens, and extraction responses average ~ 480 tokens.
- We expect to start with a pilot of 2k MAU then ramp to 25k MAU over 6 months. Peak concurrency is likely to be ~1.4% of MAU during billing cycle spikes (~350 concurrent at pilot; ~3500 at scale).

Also: some prompts include 2–3 prior messages for context (we call it the "thread history"), which pushes context up to ~1,200 tokens in worst-case. We flagged the examples in finops_sample_prompts.csv.

Let us know what model shortlist you recommend given cost and latency tradeoffs — we're sensitive to both.

—Emily
Product Lead, FinOps Analytics

Attachments: finops_sample_prompts.csv (csv), q3_traffic_snapshot.pdf (pdf)

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finops.io>, Jason Reed <jason.reed@finops.io>
Date: 2026-09-18T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Quick follow on context + volume (FinOps onboarding)

Thanks Emily — useful details. Internal note / handoff to implementation: below is a concise model shortlist and initial sizing assumptions (I'll share with CS and SRE for the kickoff).

Model shortlist (initial candidates):
- Llama-3-13B-8k (quantized) — good latency/cost balance for classification + extraction; works well with 1k–8k context.
- Redwood-extended-7B-16k (FP16) — lower inference cost for high prompt counts; prefer if we need more conversational history.
- Mistral-Instruct-7B-8k — strong instruction-following; useful for extraction quality at moderate cost.

Context depth matrix (worst-case sample):
- Prompt only: 320 tokens
- Prompt + 2 prior messages: 1,200 tokens
- Prompt + KV cache warmup window (prefetch ctx): 1,600 tokens

Traffic & token-multiplier assumptions (Emily's numbers + conservative buffers):
- Pilot (2k MAU): average daily active ~300 (15% DAU), avg requests/user/day 2.2 -> ~660 requests/day; avg tokens/request (in+out) 800 -> ~528k tokens/day.
- Ramp (25k MAU target): avg daily active ~3,750, avg requests/user/day 2.2 -> ~8,250 requests/day; tokens/day ~6.6M.
- Peak multiplier (billing cycle spikes): apply 3.5x concurrency multiplier to peak throughput planning.

Operational notes / recommendations:
- Start pilot on Llama-3-13B-8k quantized to control cost; if extraction regression appears (>2% accuracy delta) switch to Redwood-extended-7B-16k for payloads with >1,000 tokens.
- Enable automatic prefix caching for known system prompts to save 8–12% token cost.
- Configure canary rollout: 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% over 48–72 hours with regression checks on extraction F1 (sampled).

Next steps:
1) Monica — can you schedule a 60-min kickoff with FinOps for next Tues? Include CS, SRE, and one infra engineer.
2) Ben — please prepare a quick cost-estimate sketch for both pilot and 6-month ramp (tokens + reserved capacity options).
3) Grace — grab the sample prompts and run a 20-input quality snapshot across the three shortlisted models; share a one-page note.

I'll draft a short mutual action plan after we have the kickoff time.

—Vivek
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Jason Reed <jason.reed@finops.io>

On Fri, Sep 18, 2026 at 11:04 AM Vivek Khulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Emily — useful details. Internal note / handoff to implementation: below is a concise model shortlist and initial sizing assumptions ...

Thanks Vivek — that reads well. A couple of clarifications from our side that affect capacity planning:
- A/B testing: we'd like to run a phased A/B (baseline vs. extraction-tuned) with ~10% of users for the first 4 weeks — so factor an additional 10% to token volume during experiment windows.
- Retention/Replay: we will persist anonymized interactions and replay a 1% sample for daily regression checks (adds ~1.2x tokens to background batch workloads).

Given that, our preferred kickoff time is Tue 2026-09-22 at 10:00 AM PT. Please confirm attendees and share a short agenda.

Thanks,
Jason
Director of Product, FinOps Analytics
